book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Marchers who restored the flow of water

definitions.meaning: surface reading: protesters on a march, perhaps campaigning about a water supply

definitions.text: who restored the flow of water
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: the 617 Squadron airmen of 1943, famous for a march, who breached German dams

explanation.walkthrough: The 1955 film about the RAF raid on the Ruhr dams has a celebrated march as its theme; breaching the dams set the water flowing again.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dam Busters raid destroyed dams in Germany, releasing the held-back water, and its film march is very well known.

clue.text: Hot tar concoction for a sore one?

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture of ingredients stirred together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A folk remedy: a hot tarry mixture for someone with an ache.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works by filling in a phrase: a sore one is a sore throat, which a hot concoction might soothe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore throat is a common ailment, so the answer is the body part that 'a sore one' completes.

clue.text: A Frenchman, a Parisian, exchanged ends with explorer

indicators.note: exchanged means the letters of the word that follows swap places with each other

parts.note: taken as written
M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman
un is French for a
the letters of ends, rearranged

explanation.surface: Two French people swapped places at the ends of a line with an explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchanged ends' reads like trading the end letters; it is the word ends itself being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Amundsen was the Norwegian polar explorer who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole in 1911.

clue.text: Rigid court room

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
a den is a small private room

explanation.surface: A strict, formal courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court room' reads as a law court; court is the verb meaning to pursue romantically.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden can mean stiff and inflexible, like an awkward actor or a rigid manner.

clue.text: First man from Beamish or European lady in India

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the word's letters are reworked into something new
first picks out the opening letter of the word right after it

parts.note: the first letter of man
the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The first man to come from Beamish, or a European woman in colonial India: two figures from history.
explanation.walkthrough: Beamish is a village and open-air museum in County Durham. The single M and the letters of Beamish together are rearranged; 'from' is a loose anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Memsahib was the respectful term used in colonial India for a married European woman.

clue.text: Present provided inside fast car

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other piece

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, labels a fast touring car
provided can mean on condition that, which is if

explanation.surface: A gift tucked inside a sports car, as a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is something given freely to another person, which is a gift.

clue.text: Joseph preceded Bill, the man who was the father of the Virgin Mary

definitions.text: the father of the Virgin Mary

parts.note: Jo is a short form of the name Joseph
a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
the pronoun for a man as object

explanation.surface: A genealogy note: someone called Joseph came before Bill in a family line that reaches back to the Virgin Mary's father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preceded' just says the Joseph piece comes before the Bill piece. AC for account is a standard crossword abbreviation for a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian tradition names Joachim as the husband of Saint Anne and the father of Mary, mother of Jesus.

clue.text: Note punishment isn't severe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short letter or message
second meaning: a light school penalty of writing out a sentence repeatedly

explanation.walkthrough: Lines are a school punishment in which a pupil copies out a sentence many times; only a few of them is a mild sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief note is a short message, and a pupil given only a small number of lines has escaped lightly.

clue.text: Order replacement silk for pillar

indicators.note: a replacement puts things in new places, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

parts.note: the Order of the British Empire, abbreviated OBE
the letters of silk, rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to swap in new silk as a substitute for a pillar, like a decorator's odd order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order replacement' reads as placing an order for a replacement; in fact Order is the British honour and replacement signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone monument, a kind of pillar or column.

clue.text: Something to chew in church that's illuminated in Scotland

definitions.note: the definition names where the place is; it stands for a town in Scotland

parts.note: kirk is the Scottish word for a church
cud is food that cows chew again
something illuminated is lit up, so bright

explanation.surface: Chewing gum in a brightly lit church somewhere in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In church' suggests putting one piece inside another, but the pieces simply follow each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirkcudbright is a small town in Dumfries and Galloway in south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Journalist became a member and was added afterwards

parts.note: a sub, or sub-editor, is a journalist who corrects copy
to join is to become a member

explanation.surface: A reporter signed up to a club and was enrolled as a latecomer.
explanation.definitionFit: To subjoin is to append at the end, so something subjoined was attached or appended later.

clue.text: Instrument, Stradivarius is tempting a redhead initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A Stradivarius violin is so lovely it lures a red-haired player.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stradivarius pulls the mind to violins, but the instrument is the long-necked Indian one built from initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a plucked stringed instrument of Indian classical music, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Asecond TV is something advantageous

parts.note: 'A second' printed run together: A, then S for second
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: Owning a second television is a real plus in a household.
explanation.walkthrough: The book prints 'A second' as one word. S is the standard abbreviation for second.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable quality or possession, a thing that gives an advantage.

clue.text: Oddly shaped tiny chest is not real

indicators.note: something oddly shaped has been twisted out of its usual form, as the letters here are

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A strangely formed little chest turns out to be a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthetic means artificial or man-made, as opposed to natural or genuine.

clue.text: Charts river before playing with server

parts.note: charts of figures are tables
the Po is the river of northern Italy
a show that is playing is on

explanation.surface: Maps of a river come first, before a game with someone serving at tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Server' looks like a tennis player; here it is a utensil for serving food.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablespoon is a large spoon used for serving out food at table.

clue.text: Merseyside?

parts.note: surface reading: the metropolitan county around Liverpool; setter's reading: a Mersey side, a football team from the Mersey

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as 'Mersey side': a side is a sports team, and this one is a Liverpool football club, rivals of Liverpool FC.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton FC is a football club based in Liverpool, on the River Mersey, so it is a side from Merseyside.

clue.text: Idle creature on the other side

parts.note: a tick is a small blood-sucking creature
over can mean across, on the far side

explanation.surface: A lazy animal lounging somewhere across the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' reads as an adjective describing the creature; it is the verb, said of an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over runs slowly in neutral, which is what an engine does when it idles.

clue.text: I am covering Edward who is drunk

parts.note: with the lost opening I, 'I am' contracts to I'm
a bib is a covering worn over clothes while eating
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to protecting Edward, who has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' reads as a verb, shielding Edward; it is a noun, the cloth tied round a diner's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, especially alcohol, so imbibed is the past participle meaning drunk.

clue.text: 17__I leave confusingly efficient operative

indicators.note: confusingly says what remains is jumbled into a new order
to leave is to go away, so that letter departs from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written, before one letter goes
the letter itself, the one that leaves

explanation.surface: Someone quits their post, and somehow the place becomes efficient once they have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The book's OCR garbled the first word, which must be I: 'I leave' takes one of the two I's out of efficient, leaving exactly the eight letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule that is in effect is in force or working, which is what operative means of a law or arrangement.

clue.text: Failed to retain principle with hopeless endeavour

parts.note: to have lost something is to have failed to keep it
a cause is a principle one supports

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned their principles during a futile attempt at something.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is an undertaking or movement with no chance of success, a hopeless venture.

clue.text: Not due to have married one Italian first

parts.note: uno is Italian for one
to have wed is to have married

explanation.surface: Someone not expected to marry, an Italian, got there first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' tells us the Italian piece comes before the marriage piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Unowed means not owing or payable, so a sum that is unowed is not due.

clue.text: Cut vertically, say

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word for cut and hear another spelling

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as with sheep

explanation.surface: An instruction to slice something straight down, with an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut vertically' looks like one instruction; the definition is the adverb alone.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, sheer means perpendicularly, straight up or down, as a cliff drops sheer to the sea.

clue.text: Anartist has come up from a very dry place

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means reading from the bottom to the top

parts.note: 'An artist' printed run together: A for an, then RA, a Royal Academician
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist has returned from a trip to an arid region.
explanation.walkthrough: The book prints 'An artist' run together. 'has' is part of the fodder, not a link, and goes up with the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, in North Africa, and a desert is an extremely dry place.

clue.text: 'Inthe rain a poor-spirited good-for-nothing

indicators.note: in the tells us the letters sit within the run of words that comes next

parts.note: the letters straddling rain, a and poor
surface padding left over from the compound poor-spirited

explanation.surface: Someone out in the rain is a feeble, worthless wretch.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoo is First World War slang, from French il n'y en a plus, meaning finished or no good. The hyphenated poor-spirited is split, so its second half is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoo means done for, useless or worthless, which is the adjective good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Place leading navigator inside boat

indicators.note: inside means the selected letter is placed within the other piece

parts.note: to place something is to put it

indicators.note: leading picks out the letter at the front of the word that follows

parts.note: the first letter of navigator

explanation.surface: Seat the chief navigator in the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading navigator' sounds like the boat's best navigator; leading only picks out a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A punt is a flat-bottomed boat pushed along with a pole, as on rivers at Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Ready for use after hanging

parts.note: surface reading: game meat or cheese prepared by being hung up to mature; setter's reading: clothes taken straight from the rack in a shop, ready-made

explanation.walkthrough: Hanging suggests game birds left to mature, but the hanging is clothes on a shop hook, taken down and worn at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-peg describes garments bought ready-made rather than tailored, so immediately usable.

clue.text: From that time engineers had been free from pretence

parts.note: since means from that time onward
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Ever since then, the engineers had been honest and unaffected.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine and honest, without any feigning or hypocrisy.

clue.text: Motor on left side — in here perhaps

definitions.text: Motor on left side — in here perhaps

parts.note: a motor is a car
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A car parked on the left, possibly in some shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a motor parked at the side of a house, in a shelter of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A carport is a roofed shelter for a car, often open-sided and built against a house wall.
